verdicts.claim: Checkpointing transfers eligible committed page changes from the WAL into the main database; copying pages and resetting the WAL are separate
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'A checkpoint operation takes content from the WAL file and transfers it back into the original database file'; rewind of WAL described separately; Fly: copy vs 'restart the WAL file'.

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE checkpoints copy as many frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers and never invoke the busy handler; concurrent
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode ... passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers.'

verdicts.claim: The default auto-checkpoint threshold is 1000 WAL pages, configurable at compilation or through wal_autocheckpoint.
verdicts.evidence: pragma: 'Autocheckpointing is enabled by default with an interval of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT'; wal.html: 'threshold size of 1000 pages'.

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE; a nonpositive runtime threshold disables them.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'checkpoints initiated by ... the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE'; pragma: 'Setting the auto-checkpoint size to zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off.'

verdicts.claim: FULL waits for the writer and older reader snapshots ... RESTART ... TRUNCATE reduces the WAL to zero bytes. These modes block writers while allowing readers
verdicts.evidence: c3ref FULL: 'blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded'; TRUNCATE 'truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'.

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns busy status, total WAL frames, and total checkpointed frames ... -1 outside WAL mode and zero after successful TRUNCATE
verdicts.evidence: pragma: 'second and third column are -1 if there is no write-ahead log'; busy=1 only 'if a RESTART or FULL or TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked'; c3ref: after TRUNCATE 'both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero'.

verdicts.claim: With synchronous=NORMAL, WAL synchronization occurs before checkpoints and database synchronization after completed checkpoints. Unlike FULL
verdicts.evidence: pragma: 'the WAL file is synchronized before each checkpoint and the database file is synchronized after each completed checkpoint'; 'might roll back following a power loss or system crash'.

verdicts.claim: Long-lived or overlapping reader snapshots that retain WAL content can prevent complete checkpointing or WAL reset while writes continue
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from making progress' ... 'the WAL file will grow without bound'.

verdicts.claim: Normal checkpointing usually retains the allocated WAL for reuse; successful copying need not shrink its physical size. Successful TRUNCATE
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set)'; c3ref TRUNCATE truncates to zero bytes.

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: Fly.io describes RESTART/TRUNCATE as blocking new read and write transactions. SQLite's API and PRAGMA references specify
verdicts.evidence: Fly: 'You can force SQLite to block new read & write transactions so it can restart the WAL'; pragma RESTART: 'blocks concurrent writers while it is running, but allows readers to proceed'.
